material_units.source_text:
Definition — Entropy (discrete and differential), nats
      For a probability vector $p=(p_1,\dots,p_n)$, $H(p)=-\sum_ip_i\log p_i$ with $0\log0=0$. With natural logarithms the unit is the nat ($1$ nat $=1/\ln2\approx1.44$ bits). $0\le H(p)\le\log n$, with equality on the right iff $p$ is uniform: by Jensen (concave $\log$), $H=\sum_ip_i\log\frac1{p_i}\le\log\sum_{i:p_i\gt0}p_i\frac1{p_i}\le\log n$. For a density the differential entropy $h(p)=-\int p\log p$ may be negative and changes under rescaling; for $\mathcal N(m,\Sigma)$ in $\mathbb R^n$ with $\Sigma\succ0$, $h=\tfrac12\log\det(2\pi e\,\Sigma)$. Conditional entropy $H(X\mid Y)=\mathbb E_y[H(X\mid Y=y)]$ obeys the chain rule $H(X,Y)=H(Y)+H(X\mid Y)$.
